Making-of · Three.js playable ad

Scrambly Fox Playable

A cozy low-poly fox tries a new minigame every 15 seconds, earns coins, and trades them for rewards. This page explains the art direction, the prompts that steered it, the tools and pipeline, each minigame, and how it was validated.

01 · The brief

What was asked

Opening prompt (translated from Portuguese) Let's make a Three.js playable for the Scrambly app. The character is a happy low-poly fox. Main colors #f58324, #7845d8, #201338, #fff6e8. Everything in English. Must not exceed 5 MB. The catch has to happen in the first 5 seconds; the rest is about retention. Several minigames, 15 s each, a different one every play, around 5 of them. Lots of motion, VFX and SFX, haptics if possible. It opens with the fox appearing and a minigame carousel spinning above her head for a second, the fox looking confused at it, like Animal Crossing. Then the background moves away to reveal the minigame with one mission that adds value to the account. The only action completes the mission, there is a completion ceremony and the fox earns coins. Then the next one. After the second, a CTA: Discover new games, complete missions, earn rewards! Make concepts of each storyboard beat and minigame in Layer first.

Hook, first 5 s

Fox pops in, a thought-bubble carousel spins about 1.3 s and lands on a game while the fox looks confused.

Retention

Two 15 s missions, coins after each, a rewards shop, then the end card with replay. The coin balance carries over replays.

Constraints

One self-contained HTML under 5 MB, English copy, portrait and landscape, haptics where supported.

02 · Art direction

Warm, comfy, rounded

Direction settled after three fox iterations: a soft vinyl-toy fox with rounded forms and blush cheeks, in the Animal Crossing and Kirby register. Lighting is baked so the look stays soft and consistent on any phone GPU, and the camera stays low so the fox's face is always readable.

#f58324Fox orange
#7845d8Scrambly purple
#201338Deep night
#fff6e8Cream
#ffc53aCoin gold

Storyboard concepts

Style rules applied in the build

RuleHow it is implemented
Soft, baked lightThe fox texture is baked in Blender Cycles (warm key + lavender rim). Props get a world-space light bake into vertex colours at scene load. Everything renders unlit: no runtime lights.
Readable faceAnimal Crossing-style camera, low and close. When idle, the fox turns 3/4 toward the camera. Expressions swap on a face decal (UV offset into a 3×2 atlas).
Painted worldGrounds and backdrops are Layer paintings (meadow, garden, snow, arena, cabin, candy sky), not flat colours.
Chunky UIFredoka type, cream pills, purple tags, orange buttons, gold coins. The mission card is centred at the top with an orange glow and appears large before it settles.

Who did what

ToolUsed for
Claude Opus 5.5 in Claude CodePlanning, all code (Three.js, esbuild, Blender and Python scripts), prompt writing for Layer, visual review of every screenshot, and orchestration of parallel subagents (layout, animation, VFX, props, QA).

Blender CLIWeld, decimate, rig and skin fixes, lighting bake, face-decal cut, export. See the next sections.
gltf-transform · ffmpeg · PillowGLB quantization; audio trimming and frame extraction; chroma key and sprite cutting.
Three.js · esbuildRuntime; bundles everything (models, WebP, MP3, font) into one HTML.

Also tried: Uthana and Tripo Animate through Layer, which failed on the provider side, and a 2D-sprite fox built from Layer videos, which was dropped in favour of the 3D fox.

04 · Asset pipeline

From prompt to playable

Layer concept→Layer front render (magenta bg)→Meshy / Tripo image-to-3D→Blender CLI: weld · decimate · rig · bake→gltf-transform quantize→esbuild inline→dist/index.html
05 · Blender CLI

Reduce, rig, bake, export

All mesh work runs headless, so any asset can be regenerated with one command.

# fox: merge Meshy's clip GLBs, weld + decimate, reweight the head, bake light, cut the face decal
blender -b -P tools/blender/anim.py -- assets/models/fox_anim_rigged.glb \
  idle=assets/raw/anim/idle.glb

# props: weld, decimate to a triangle budget, bake soft light, 256–512 px JPEG textures
bash tools/props_build.sh            # all 16 props (or name the ones to rebuild)

# quantize for mobile (Node 20+)
gltf-transform quantize assets/models/fox_anim_rigged.glb assets/models/fox.glb

# face expressions atlas (Python + Pillow)
python3 tools/face_atlas.py

# bundle everything into one HTML (fails above 5 MB)
npm run build
StepWhat it doesWhy
Weld (merge by distance 0.0005)Joins Meshy's split UV-seam vertices before decimationDecimating unwelded seams opened 3,631 holes; after welding: 6, the same as the source.
Decimate (ratio 0.35)12,437 → 4,351 triangles, then smooth shadingMobile budget ("too high poly").
RigMeshy Rigging skeleton (Hips, Spine, Head, arms, legs); an early custom rig used auto weightsBones for procedural posing.
Head reweightEverything above the neck follows the Head bone only, with a short blend bandWaving an arm was squashing the cheeks by up to 14.5% of body height; now 0%.
Bake (Cycles, diffuse)Warm key + lavender rim + sky, baked into a 1024 px textureThe game renders unlit: lighting is baked.
Face decalA copy of the face faces with planar UVs, plus a front render used to paint expressionsExpressions by UV swap, as requested.
AnimationProcedural poses on the rig in Three.js (per-state targets, spring follow, squash and stretch)Meshy preset clips (dance, sword…) were too busy for the minimal cartoon style.
06 · Playable flow

30 seconds of cozy

Fox pops in→Carousel spins, fox confused→Wipe reveal→Mission appears big, then settles at the top→15 s play→Mission complete +50 / Time's up +25→2nd minigame→Rewards shop: claim or continue→End card + replay
BehaviourDecision
Minigame orderGames not played yet in the session come first; never the same one twice in a row.
Timer runs outNo automatic win. "Time's up" offers Try again or Skip; skipping pays a +25 consolation.
BackgroundTab hidden or window blurred: game clock, animations and audio pause, then resume.
CTADemo build: logs CTA clicked - demo only. The top-right corner stays empty for the network's close button; replay is bottom left, above mute.
No WebGLFalls back to a 2D flow (carousel → end card) without granting coins.

08 · Economy

Always a reward to collect

A win pays 50 coins and a time's-up pays 25, so every run of two missions earns at least 50. The shop always offers a Gift Card (50), a Mystery Box (100) and a Mega Gift Card (150). Claiming deducts the price, and Continue leaves at any time. Once nothing more is affordable, the shop goes straight to the CTA. The balance carries over replays and resets on refresh.

09 · Prompt log

How the work was steered

User prompts from the session, translated to English where they were in Portuguese, with the decision each one led to.

StyleThe playable's overall style should be very warm, comfy and rounded, in the Animal Crossing and Kirby vein.→ Fox v2: rounded vinyl-toy look, soft light, blush cheeks.
StyleMore minimalist and stylized: low poly with simple shapes, Animal Crossing style, expression in the eyes and eyebrows, a simple cartoony mouth.→ Generated v3a/v3b; the user then chose v2 ("v2 was better").
LayoutYou can do portrait and landscape.→ Every concept and screen is designed for both orientations.
NamingThe minigames need fake names as if they were published games.→ Forest Crush, Merge Meadow, Slime Survivors, Frostfire Camp, Cub Rush 3D, Blaster Buddies, Treehouse Stack, Fox Fishing.
BuildNow build the playable with Three.js: make the model, the animations and the 2D assets according to the concepts.→ Three.js + esbuild single-file build with a headless Playwright harness.
AssetsWhat about the assets, weren't they generated in Layer to use? The finished assets, like the concepts.→ Moved to Layer-generated finals: Meshy fox, UI kit, icons, items, backgrounds.
LookThe lighting is kind of ugly, and the character has no facial animation. It can be simple animations, just swapping UVs.→ Face decal plus expression atlas via UV offset, and blinking.
LookYou can bake all the lighting of the models. In the 2D parts, use the 2D asset with animations.→ Cycles bake for the fox, vertex-colour bake for props; 2D fox poses on the hub and end card.
AudioGenerate a little music with sound, SFX and so on.→ Lyria 3 music loop and 15 Sonilo SFX, with a WebAudio synth fallback.
RetentionIt still isn't clear that these missions can be traded for rewards… maybe open the store?→ Reward meter next to the coins, a "Play games › Earn coins › Get rewards" tagline, and the Rewards Shop.
QATest portrait 320×568 and 390×844, landscape 568×320 and 844×390. When the page is in the background, pause the clock and gameplay and mute automatically. Test in multiple browsers.→ Pause on visibility and blur; Playwright matrix across three engines and four sizes.
3DThe character is entirely broken, the mesh has gaps, and the animation loops, crossfades and transitions are not polished.→ Measured the cause (decimation of unwelded seams) and fixed it by welding first; clip cleanup; later moved to procedural poses.
3DLet's focus on the 3D version. Adjust the camera to be more like an Animal Crossing camera, where the character's face is always easy to spot, not too much from above.→ Lower cameras in every game, and the fox turns 3/4 toward the camera when idle.
3DAnimations are deforming the mesh way too much, like an arm waving reducing the cheeks.→ Head reweighted to the Head bone only; deformation measured at 0%.
GamesLet's build more minigames and make the balance accumulate through reruns.→ Added Blaster Buddies, Treehouse Stack and Fox Fishing; balance carries over replays.
GamesMake the minigames not win automatically when the timer runs out.→ Time's up with Try again or Skip.
GamesFor each minigame, make more interactions, not just one swipe or one hit.→ Multi-step missions: 3 matches, 3 merges, 3 gates plus boss, 5 rooms, 3 fish.
ShopWhen the trade-up overlay comes, it seems the player is forced to buy something. Maybe have two possible actions, claim or continue.→ Claim and Continue buttons; no automatic claim.
ArtImprove the animations: in fishing the character stays in T-pose. VFX are not implemented. Enemies and scenery are too low poly instead of being generated by Layer.→ Contextual poses, Layer VFX flipbooks and 16 Layer/Tripo props, in three parallel subagents.
EconomyChange the economy so that the player will always have a reward to collect. The coin deduction doesn't seem quite correct either.→ Win +50, time's-up +25, shop prices 50/100/150, and claiming deducts the price exactly.
ShopAfter everything is consumed in the trade-up, just automatically show the CTA. The close button normally goes where the restart is; maybe move it on top of the mute.→ The shop closes by itself once nothing more is affordable; replay moved above mute, leaving the top-right corner free for the ad network's close button.
AnimationThe animation does not seem integrated, given the procedural poses shown on the QA board.→ Logged the fox state in every game and cropped the fox at key moments: the poses were set but not readable. Fixed facing (3/4 toward the camera), the watering timing and the beanie, plus a Merge freeze found along the way.
PolishMissions are not highlighted and centred on top.→ Centred at the top in both orientations, orange glow, and a big intro before it settles.

Every result below comes from a script in tools/ and can be re-run. Screenshots were reviewed after every change.

All 8 minigames winnablepass
A bot plays each game by its own rules and wins in 3.3–9.7 s of the 15 s timer, with 0 errors.
Always a rewardpass
Win, time-out, win: every shop visit had a claim; claims deduct exactly.
Time's up is not a winpass
Time's up → +25 → shop → Continue → end card, 0 errors.
Browsers × sizespass
Chromium, Firefox, WebKit at 320×568, 390×844, 568×320, 844×390, 0 errors.
Background pausepass
Tab hidden and window blur: clock 0 s, audio suspended, both resume.
Rotationpass
Every scene re-lays out portrait ↔ landscape.
Mesh and rigpass
6 open edges (was 3,631); head deformation 0% (was 14.5%).
Shop → CTApass
Claiming all affordable rewards opens the end card in 1.3 s (portrait and landscape).
Poses visible in-gamepass
State log + fox crops per game; fixed facing, the watering timing and a Merge freeze when merging in the first 0.5 s.

4.34 MB single HTML (limit 5 MB).
